A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same structured-sparse matrix multiplication benchmark and CUDA kernel. All 23 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including figures, equations and appendices, support comparison across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: Sections 3–6 and Appendix B report original GPU runtime measurements, energy measurements and ViT inference timings, including supplementary half-precision experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains the original GPU runtime, energy and ViT inference results in Sections 3–6 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: V2 Algorithms 1 and 2 correspond to v1 Algorithms 2 and 1. The sparsity support, indexed multiplications, single CUDA kernel and Appendix D optimizations remain equivalent. Renaming butterfly factors as Kronecker-sparse matrices and emphasizing tiling do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic structured-matrix benchmarks, ViT-S/16 submodules and ViT-S/B/L/H timing scenarios. The terminology change does not introduce different data, tasks or evaluated matrix families.

E2.justification: Corresponding matrix comparisons retain bmm, einsum, bsr, dense and generic CSR sparse implementations. ViT comparisons retain bmm and fully-connected implementations. Added citations and baseline source attribution do not introduce additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The 600-pattern benchmark, matrix batch size of 25,088, image batch size of 128, initialization distributions, precision settings and memory layouts remain unchanged. V2's explicit two-factor ViT replacement description was already documented in v1 Appendix B.7.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the memory-rewriting estimates, matrix-size comparisons, memory-layout analysis, linear-layer timing decomposition and half-precision experiments. The new discussion of pattern selection introduces an interpretation, not an additional ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 retains at least 10 measurements of 10 runs for timing and 10 measurements of at least 16 runs for energy. Median and IQR reporting, boxplot quartiles and 5th/95th-percentile whiskers are unchanged.

E6.justification: V1's conclusion attaches a median reduction factor of ×0.85 to its speed claim; v2 removes that quantitative speed statement while retaining ×0.85 as the energy reduction in Section 5. The numerical tables and empirical plots otherwise match, including the 88.10% FP32 win rate and ×1.39 median acceleration among wins. This changes the summary reporting, not the measured results.

T1.justification: V2 removes Appendix C.2's block-butterfly definitions, equivalence Lemma C.4 and its proof and derivations. The corresponding matrix-family entry moves from v1 Table 8 to v2 Table 1 without that justification. The support definition, perfect-shuffle identity and proof, and memory-rewriting ratio remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The benchmark, kernel acceleration and inference claims remain central. V2 adds contribution (iii), presenting (b+c)/bc as a heuristic for selecting patterns efficient relative to dense matrices, and foregrounds tiling as the contribution. The introduction also replaces the near-linear complexity description with a sub-quadratic one.

C2.justification: V2 Section 4.3 extends the existing correlation between the rewriting ratio and kernel advantage into guidance for neural-network architecture design. Conversely, it drops v1 Section 4's detailed explanation connecting contiguous column accesses to batch-size-last efficiency. The half-precision and hardware-extension perspectives remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit links to the project's implementation and the cited einsum source, whereas v1 announces an open-source kernel without a project URL. Appendix B's software, hardware and measurement details and Appendix D's implementation listings and optimizations are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Han et al.'s Deep Compression and Zheng et al.'s rank-one-block identification paper, and removes the SIDUS reference with the acknowledgments. It motivates its terminology by discussing limitations of existing butterfly definitions and describes its benchmark as complementary to prior reports in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around Kronecker-sparse matrices. Background and kernel explanations are reorganized, algorithm numbering is exchanged, and Section 4 becomes three subsections incorporating material previously in Sections 2 and 3. These are extensive narrative changes despite stable experiments.

P2.justification: The document is retypeset with different typography, title treatment and page format. Figure 2 gains colored weights and explanatory labels; the algorithm and memory-flow illustrations are revised. V1 Table 8 moves into the main text as v2 Table 1, and Figure 18 is removed. Empirical plot graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies support-only sparsity, reorganizes the kernel explanation and adds explicit code access. However, it removes the block-butterfly equivalence proof while retaining that example, and promotes the existing ratio into a broader pattern-selection claim against dense matrices, although Figure 6 establishes relative kernel performance against specialized baselines. These accessibility gains and losses or uncertainties in justification leave the net quality change unclear.
